description:
CHECKPOINT 2026-08-19/20: the Zhu-Hawari generalized coherent-elastic
implementation landed and is real -- commit 8933cdbf on develop. Not fully
closed out; this bead tracks what remains.

WHAT LANDED. crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/coher.rs split into
coher/{mod,builtin,crystals,general}.rs. general.rs adds
coher_general_with_constants(), a general reciprocal-lattice Bragg-edge sum
taking an arbitrary CrystalStructure (lattice cell + basis atoms + coherent
scattering lengths), rather than the 6 hardcoded built-in lattices in
builtin.rs. Wired into leapr::generate so tsl-CinSiC.leapr (MAT 44) and
tsl-SiinSiC.leapr (MAT 43) now produce a real MF=7/MT=2 coherent-elastic
section.

MEASURED (release build, 0.0253 eV / 296 K):
  C in SiC (MAT 44):  elastic 2.853825 b vs oracle 2.94078 b  (-2.96%)
  Si in SiC (MAT 43): elastic 2.853825 b vs oracle 2.94078 b  (-2.96%)
Both materials produce the IDENTICAL elastic value -- confirmed correct,
since coherent elastic is a lattice property of the 3C-SiC compound as a
whole (see reference-data/endf/README.md's double-counting note), not a
per-sublattice one. Test:
crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/tests/leapr_sic_coherent_elastic_oracle.rs
(3 tests, all passing: two 5%-tolerance oracle comparisons + one identity
check pinning the double-counting trap).

NOT YET DONE (this bead tracks it):
  1. Root-cause the ~3% gap vs the oracle. Candidates noted but not
     investigated: Debye-Waller treatment, form-factor approximation, a
     missing higher-order reflection, or a lattice-constant/basis
     transcription slip in crystals.rs's SiliconCarbide3C definition (human
     re-verify required per the existing LatticeConstants convention in
     builtin.rs).
  2. Full edge-by-edge Bragg-energy comparison against the oracle tape's 1044
     MT=2 records -- currently only the single cumulative thermal-point value
     (0.0253 eV) is checked, not the whole spectrum.
  3. crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs's two gap
     tests (sic_carbon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck,
     sic_silicon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck) are
     #[ignore]d with the measured numbers recorded in their doc comments, NOT
     rewritten to a real assertion. They need a proper tolerance-based
     rewrite (mirroring triso_carbon_coatings_bind_graphite_sab's pattern)
     once (1) and (2) give enough confidence to pin a number.
  4. self-consistency diagnostic
     (leapr_coher_general_self_consistency.rs, #[ignore]d, run with
     --ignored) shows the general path agrees with the existing 6 built-in
     lattices to ~1e-10 relative at LOW energy but diverges up to O(1)
     relative by 5 eV -- not root-caused, may be related to (1) or may be a
     genuine algorithmic difference (edge count / cutoff) between the two
     paths. Needs investigation before the general path can be trusted to
     replace builtin.rs's hardcoded lattices even for the 6 known ones.
  5. Zhu & Hawari's ICNC 2015 companion paper (OSTI 23100909), cited
     alongside the 2014 thesis as describing the same formulation more
     concisely, is still not located as a free PDF and not catalogued in
     kovan-literature. The 2014 thesis (now catalogued,
     crates/kovan-literature/open/theses/zhu2014thermal.{json,pdf}) was the
     only source used for this implementation.
  6. V&V documentation per the root CLAUDE.md V&V rule is currently only in
     the test files' doc comments (methodology + results, as required) --
     no docs/ entry yet for this crate's development-history record. Add one
     if/when this bead closes.
  7. triso_particle.rs's module doc was updated to reflect the new state but
     says explicitly "not yet fully verified" -- flip that language only once
     (1)-(3) are resolved.

Mirrors GitHub issue #24 / bead op-t33q. Depends on op-jw4a (implementation);
this bead is the "finish the job properly" follow-up.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-08-21 context for item (1), root-causing the ~3% elastic gap: the
INELASTIC half of the same material is now proven exact, which usefully
narrows where the elastic discrepancy can live.

Measured (commit 1a904fc5): regenerating Si-in-SiC from its deck reproduces
the published ENDF/B-VIII.0 MT=4 kernel at all 8 declared temperatures --
306,033 points, worst 0.0000%, T_eff exact. So the deck parsing, the alpha/
beta grids, the phonon expansion, the Debye-Waller/effective-temperature
machinery and the endout writer are all faithful for this material.

Like-for-like at 300 K, sigma at 0.0253 eV (b/atom):
  elastic    deck 2.85169  vs tape 2.94078   -> -3.03%   <- the open gap
  inelastic  deck 0.066150 vs tape 0.066150  -> +0.0000%

Since dwpix/T_eff feed BOTH channels and the inelastic channel is exact, a
Debye-Waller error is now an unlikely explanation for the elastic gap --
it would have to be confined to the elastic path's own use of it (note
generate.rs computes a separate dwpix_elastic via compound_debye_waller for
the generalized path). That, the form-factor/structure-factor sum, and the
3C-SiC lattice constants in coher/crystals.rs are the remaining candidates.

Also note the earlier "-2.96%" figure in this bead was measured at 293.6 K;
at 300 K like-for-like it is -3.03%.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-21. The -3.03% elastic residual is NOT a defect in this port -- it is a property of the published ENDF/B-VIII.0 evaluation.

METHOD. Item 2 (full edge-by-edge comparison) done, and it answers item 1. Every SiC Bragg edge, published or regenerated, sits at E = n*E1 with n = h^2+k^2+l^2 on the conventional cell's simple-cubic reciprocal lattice (E1 = 1.066463 meV, the (100) spacing of a = 4.379 A), so n keys the two tables together independently of lattice constant, constants vintage and Debye-Waller treatment. Compared which reflections are extinguished.

RESULT (n <= 100, release, vs reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf):
  zinc-blende (what we ship):  35 reflections live in both, 25 EXTINCTION MISMATCHES
  'edge-centred' basis:        60 reflections live in both,  0 extinction mismatches

The tape carries a LIVE (100) reflection at 1.066463e-3 eV, plus live (210), (300)/(221), (320), (410)/(322), ... -- every mixed-parity reflection with ODD h+k+l, all of which zinc-blende extinguishes exactly. It extinguishes every mixed-parity reflection with EVEN h+k+l. That selection rule is the signature of the structure factor S = 1 + e^{i.pi.h} + e^{i.pi.k} + e^{i.pi.l}, whose |S|^2 is 16/4/0/4 for zero/one/two/three odd indices against fcc's 16/0/0/16. S is what you get from centring translations (1/2,0,0),(0,1/2,0),(0,0,1/2) -- 'half along each axis' -- instead of the fcc (0,1/2,1/2),(1/2,0,1/2),(1/2,1/2,0) -- 'half along each PAIR of axes'.

That basis is not a possible crystal: centring translations must be closed under addition mod the lattice for the atoms they generate to be symmetry-equivalent, and (1/2,0,0)+(0,1/2,0) = (1/2,1/2,0) is not a member. Pinned by its own test.

Feeding that basis through our own general path moves the thermal-point cross section 2.83347 -> 2.91289 b against the tape's 2.94078 b (all with the tape's own fitted 4W' = 5.977/eV) -- about 2.8 of the 3.0 percentage points.

REMAINING ~1%. Sits entirely in the weak |b_Si - b_C|^2 difference reflections (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4), running high +6.1% at n=20 rising monotonically to +23.5% at n=100. Growth with tau^2 confined to the difference reflections is the signature of a PER-ATOM-TYPE Debye-Waller factor in the evaluation (Zhu's 'exact' option) vs our single compound coefficient (Zhu's 'cubic approximation'). Separately the DW coefficients differ: 4W' = 5.977/eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382/eV (ours, 296 K), ~10% apart after temperature scaling -- not root-caused.

DECISION: we KEEP the physically correct zinc-blende structure and deliberately do NOT reproduce the tape. The 5% oracle band now brackets a known, characterised bias; tightening it would mean reproducing the evaluation's error.

ITEM 4 was already root-caused and the header was just stale: the general-vs-builtin divergence at 5 eV is NJOY's fixed index box (leapr.f90:2698,2725) not enclosing the tau^2 <= econ*Emax sphere, so the BUILT-IN path drops edges above ~0.8-1 eV. Asserted with measured ratios by general.rs::builtin_index_boxes_truncate_above_their_own_lattices_reach. Header corrected.

ITEM 3 done: both outram-mc-libs gap tests un-ignored and rewritten as live tolerance assertions.

ITEM 5 (Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015 PDF) still not located -- left open, see follow-up bead.

ALL FINDINGS ARE AI-ASSISTED DRAFT. The central claim is about a published evaluation and needs human review before being cited or reported upstream.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
CLOSING this bead: every tracked item is done or split out.
  Item 1 (root-cause) - ANSWERED, see previous comment. Traced to the published evaluation's atomic basis, not to this port.
  Item 2 (edge-by-edge) - DONE, it is what answered item 1. Three new V&V tests pin it.
  Item 3 (rewrite the two gap tests) - DONE. Both un-ignored, live tolerance assertions against a documented +-5% characterised band. triso_shell_thermal_scattering now 4 passed / 1 ignored (was 2 passed / 2 ignored).
  Item 4 (general-vs-builtin divergence) - was ALREADY root-caused; only the header was stale. NJOY's fixed index box truncates the BUILT-IN path above ~1 eV. Header corrected.
  Item 5 (Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015) - split out to op-gzws with the per-atom-type Debye-Waller work.

Commit fa83715e, pushed to develop. njoy capped suite 621 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored (exit 0); cargo check --workspace --lib --tests clean.

GitHub issue #28 STAYS OPEN deliberately, at the maintainer's direction: the central finding is a claim about a published ENDF/B-VIII.0 evaluation, it is AI-assisted draft output with no human review, and the maintainer wants domain experts to check it before it is cited or reported upstream. The three questions posed to reviewers are in the issue comment. Nothing has been reported upstream.

title: LEAPR SiC coherent-elastic: root-cause ~3% oracle gap, tighten V&V, rewrite the two gap tests properly

description:
Pipeline run for HTR-10. Simulator construction is op-jyyp (18 children, 0 done) — this child is the VALIDATION run through the pipeline, and depends on it rather than duplicating it.

BENCHMARK. IAEA CRP-3 core-physics benchmark. dt-engine src/htr10/design.rs already carries Htr10DesignPoint::iaea_benchmark() with cited constants and published reference eigenvalues — the acceptance band comes from there, not from us.
TARGETS: initial criticality (critical loading height), control-rod worth, fuel and moderator temperature coefficients separately, then the DLOFC/PLOFC safety-demonstration transient, which is the HTR-10 result the literature is actually about.
ENDF NEEDED: U-235, U-238 (have), O-16, B-10 (missing); graphite and SiC TSLs (have).
HARDEST STAGE: MC. Double heterogeneity — TRISO in pebble in bed — is the defining difficulty. pebble_beds::delta_tracking and crp_packing are the CE side. State a particle x generation budget and a wall-clock ceiling before running; this is orders of magnitude past a bare sphere and cannot be scoped by analogy to one.
NOTE: op-jyyp.10, .16 and .8 are open defects (TRISO release test asserts against itself; zbs has zero tests; decay heat self-flagged suspect). Any number produced here inherits them.

Parent: op-wpi0

notes.content: The DEM -> packing -> CSG -> MC workflow this validation run needs is scoped in op-211e / gh:#54. Note the hybrid constraint recorded there: explicit CSG for pebble centres, IMPLICIT delta-tracking for TRISO inside each pebble. HTR-10 is ~27,000 pebbles x ~11,000 TRISO — explicit surfaces for that are impossible, not merely slow.

description: GH #37 §I (core CAD). Blender's 'Snap Utilities Line' add-on: place connected vertices with live vertex/edge/face/edge-center/perpendicular/tangent snapping, incremental snap, numeric length & angle entry, auto-cut through crossed faces. Depends on the snapping engine + knife.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: snap_line.rs: LineTool connected-polyline operator. add_raw / add_snapped (via snap::snap_point) / add_polar (length+angle in a WorkPlane) / add_constrained (snap then override length and/or angle, previous point as anchor); undo, close (cyclic), segment_count. commit_wire appends the polyline to a base mesh as an edge wire. auto_cut_chords emits knife::Chord for segments whose both endpoints snapped to edges of one common face (t computed by projection); general multi-face surface-walking projection deferred, as in knife.rs. 6 tests, clippy-clean.
